cim: USC helps seniors learn how to use artificial intelligence
cim_eredeti: USC helps seniors learn how to use artificial intelligence
szoveg_eredeti:
COLUMBIA, S.C. (WSPA) – The University of South Carolina hosted a workshop Friday to help seniors learn to use artificial intelligence.

The free workshop, called Safe AI for Seniors, helped explain the technology to adults over 55. This was also the second time USC hosted the event.

Panels covered AI’s role in topics such as cybersecurity and mental health.

“It’s not about just speaking more about the problems every day. We don’t want to just keep amplifying problems. We also want to shed light on what possible solutions might be there, not only locally but also best practices from around the world,” said Dr. Biplav Srivastava, a professor at USC’s AI Institute.

The workshop ran from 9:30 a.m. until just before 4 p.m.

Kicking off the day was 11-year-old speaker Harsh Vardhan, who became fascinated with AI after using it to help with his fourth-grade model rocket project.

“AI is a tool and a weapon, it’s like a kitchen knife. You can use it to cook vegetables, but you can also cut yourself,” said Vardhan. “You can ask AI for quick questions or simple tips, but other people can use it to make scams and deepfakes. It can really end up harming you.”

Panelists also warned about AI-generated phone calls designed to steal personal information or falsely claim a loved one is in trouble and needs money immediately.
